mainTopic: When does a female animal set aside for a male-only קרבן get קדושת הגוף and make a תמורה? The amud covers רבי שמעון's view, its reasons, and how רבי יהושע relates to it.
overview: This amud discusses a female animal set aside for a קרבן that must be male. The question is whether it is holy enough to make a תמורה. The תנא קמא says it always makes a תמורה. רבי שמעון says this is true only for an עולה, not for a פסח or an אשם. His reason is that only an animal that must graze until it gets a blemish can make a תמורה. רבי disagrees with him about the פסח, because a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים, which may be female. The גמרא explains why רבי does not argue about the אשם too. It then tests the idea that a female counts for an עולה because a bird עולה can be female, using the cases of the פרה אדומה and the goats of a יחיד and a נשיא. That idea is defended through רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who allows anyone who pledges an עולה to bring a bird. Finally, a משנה about dedicating all one's possessions leads רבי חייא בר אבא to question רבי יהושע's ruling. רבי יוחנן answers that רבי יהושע follows רבי שמעון's rule, and רבי חייא בר אבא begins to push back, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: First opinion: a female set aside for פסח or אשם still creates a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא finishes his ruling. Even when a female animal is set aside for a פסח or an אשם, it can create a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If someone set aside a female animal] for his פסח or for his אשם, it makes a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The text picks up in the middle of the תנא קמא's ruling. He says that a female animal set aside for a פסח or an אשם can still turn an exchanged animal into a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח and an אשם can only come from male animals, so a female cannot actually be brought. Even so, the תנא קמא holds that the female becomes fully holy with קדושת הגוף. Because of that, it has the power to create a תמורה, just like the עולה case mentioned right before.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: a regular animal someone tried to swap for a holy animal, which then becomes holy itself.
The קרבן פסח, which must be a male lamb or kid.
A guilt offering, which must be a male ram.
A female animal. This is the case under discussion.

phrases.english: And for his Paschal offering and for his guilt offering —
phrases.notes: The case is someone who set aside a female animal, even though a פסח and an אשם must be male.

phrases.english: it makes a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the תנא קמא's ruling from the previous part of the daf, where the עולה case was already given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female animal set aside for a פסח or an אשם makes a תמורה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון splits the cases: עולה yes, פסח and אשם no
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון agrees about the עולה, but says that a female set aside for a פסח or an אשם does not create a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: for his עולה, it makes a תמורה. For his פסח or his אשם, it does not make a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the תנא קמא. He draws a line between the עולה and the other two קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an עולה, a female has some connection, because a bird עולה can be female. That gives the animal real holiness, so it can create a תמורה. For a פסח or an אשם, a female never has any place at all. So the animal only gets money-value holiness (קדושת דמים) and cannot create a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering. A bird עולה may even be female.
Holiness only of the animal's value. The animal itself may be sold.
Holiness of the animal's body itself.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying the female is ordinary, unholy food. It is still holy, but only for its value (קדושת דמים). That kind of holiness is not strong enough to create a תמורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
for his burnt offering — it makes a substitute,
for his Paschal offering and his guilt offering —
it does not make a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא on the פסח and אשם cases, while agreeing on the עולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female set aside for an עולה makes a תמורה. A female set aside for a פסח or an אשם does not.

steps.title: The reason: only an animal that must graze until blemished makes a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון gives the rule behind his view. Only an animal with body-holiness, which must be left to graze until it gets a blemish, can create a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For nothing makes a תמורה except an animal that must graze until it becomes blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: This line explains the reason behind רבי שמעון's split. It is a general rule about which holy animals can create a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal with קדושת הגוף cannot simply be sold. It must wait in the pasture until it gets a מום, and only then can it be redeemed. That is the sign of real holiness, and only that kind of animal can create a תמורה. The female set aside for an עולה fits this rule, but the female set aside for a פסח or an אשם does not, because it may be sold right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Grazing until it gets a blemish. This is the treatment for a holy animal that cannot be brought but cannot be sold either.
A blemish that disqualifies an animal from the מזבח.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's test: if the animal must 'graze until blemished,' it has body-holiness and makes a תמורה. If it may be sold right away, it does not.

phrases.english: for there is nothing that makes a substitute,
except that which grazes until it becomes blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה אֶלָּא הָרוֹעֶה לְהִסְתָּאֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the underlying principle for רבי שמעון's ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an animal with body-holiness, which must graze until blemished, can create a תמורה.

steps.title: רבי rejects רבי שמעון's view about the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי disagrees with רבי שמעון only about the פסח. A leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים, and a שלמים can be female, so a female set aside for a פסח should create a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: I do not accept רבי שמעון's words regarding the פסח, since a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי steps in and rejects רבי שמעון's ruling, but only for the פסח case. He uses רבי שמעון's own rule to reach a different result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of מותר הפסח says that a פסח animal not used on פסח is brought as a שלמים. A שלמים may come from a female, so a female set aside for a פסח has a real path to the מזבח. That gives it body-holiness, so by רבי שמעון's own test it must graze until blemished and should make a תמורה. רבי says nothing against רבי שמעון's view of the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover פסח: an animal set aside for a פסח that was not offered as one.
Peace offerings. They may be brought from male or female animals.
'I do not see,' meaning 'I do not accept' someone's view.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one תנא can accept another's principle (the grazing test) and still reject how it is applied, by pointing out a fact that changes the case.

phrases.english: Rabbi said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: I do not see (accept) the words of Rabbi Shimon regarding the Paschal offering,
since a leftover Paschal offering
is sacrificed as a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי שמעון's ruling (step 2) for the פסח case, using his own principle (step 3).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial. It rejects רבי שמעון only regarding the פסח, not the אשם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי שמעון overlooked that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים, which may be female. So a female set aside for a פסח does have body-holiness.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי also argue about the אשם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי: by his own logic he should also argue with רבי שמעון about the אשם, since a leftover אשם is brought as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי also say: I don't agree with רבי שמעון about the אשם, since a leftover אשם is brought as an עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי argued only about the פסח. The same reasoning seems to work for the אשם too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's logic was that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים, which can be female. In the same way, a leftover אשם becomes an עולה, and a bird עולה can be female. So a female set aside for an אשם should also make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover אשם, for example an animal set aside for an אשם that was not needed
And let him say: the גמרא suggests what someone should have said

phrases.english: And let him say: I do not see (agree with)
the words of Rabbi Shimon regarding an אשם,
since a leftover אשם is brought as an עולה!
phrases.notes: Animal עולות must be male, but a bird עולה can be female. That is why this link would matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא: אֵין אֲנִי רוֹאֶה דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי's own פסח reasoning to the אשם and asks why he did not argue there too.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's choice to argue with רבי שמעון only about the פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A leftover אשם becomes an עולה, just as a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים. So the same logic should apply to the אשם.

steps.title: רבי holds that leftover אשם money goes to communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי follows the רבנן: leftover offerings go to the public's gift offerings, and public offerings cannot make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds like the רבנן, who say leftovers go to communal gift offerings, and there is no תמורה for communal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי, a leftover אשם does not become a private עולה at all. It goes to the public's offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, a leftover אשם is sold and the money buys communal gift offerings. A communal offering cannot make a תמורה. So the leftover אשם gives no reason to say a female אשם makes a תמורה, and רבי has no reason to argue there.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal gift offerings, brought on the מזבח when it is otherwise empty
Communal offerings cannot make a תמורה
Leftovers: money or animals set aside for an offering that were not used

steps.whatToRemember: רבי argues only about the פסח, because a leftover פסח becomes a private שלמים. A leftover אשם, according to the רבנן, goes to communal offerings, which never make a תמורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi holds like the Rabbis,
who say: leftovers go to communal gift offerings,
and there is no תמורה for a communal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying which opinion רבי holds about where leftover offerings go
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A leftover אשם becomes a private עולה, so a female אשם should make a תמורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, a leftover אשם goes to communal offerings, which cannot make a תמורה. So there is no reason to argue about the אשם.

steps.title: A suggested reason for רבי שמעון's view about the עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון says a female set aside for an עולה makes a תמורה because a bird עולה can be female.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think רבי שמעון's reason, for someone who sets aside a female for his עולה, is this: it makes a תמורה because the name 'עולה' can fit a female, as with a bird עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at רבי שמעון's own view and suggests a reason for it. This is a setup: the next steps will test this reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agreed that a female set aside for an עולה makes a תמורה, even though an animal עולה must be male. The suggested reason is that females are not totally foreign to the עולה category, because a bird עולה can be female. The words קא סלקא דעתך show this is only a first idea that is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind: a first suggestion that will probably be challenged
A bird עולה, which may be male or female
The name or status of an עולה applies to it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. It is a suggestion that the גמרא is about to attack.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind
that this is the reason of Rabbi Shimon
about one who sets aside a female for his עולה,
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 2, where רבי שמעון agreed with the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: that because of this it makes a תמורה:
since the name 'עולה' applies to it
in the case of a bird עולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי's view back to the reason behind רבי שמעון's ruling about the עולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested reason: a female set aside for an עולה makes a תמורה because there is a female kind of עולה, the bird עולה.

steps.title: Then the כהן גדול's cow should also make a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: If the bird עולה reason is right, a cow set aside by the כהן גדול instead of his bull should also count, since there is a female חטאת, the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a כהן גדול who set aside a cow for his bull: it should become holy, since there is the פרת חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason suggested in step 7 by applying it to another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול must bring a male bull as a חטאת. If any female version of a category is enough, a cow should count, because the פרה אדומה is female and is called a חטאת. Yet we do not say that, so the reason seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: introduces an attack that shows where a suggestion would lead
The פרה אדומה, which is female and is called a חטאת
Let it become holy, here meaning holy enough to make a תמורה

phrases.english: But if so,
a High Priest who set aside a cow for his bull —
phrases.notes: This is his יום כיפור bull, brought as a חטאת, which must be male.

phrases.english: let it be holy, since there is the cow of the חטאת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason suggested in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested reason: a female counts if any female version of that offering type exists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פרה אדומה is a female חטאת, so a cow set aside instead of the כהן גדול's bull should make a תמורה.

steps.title: The פרה אדומה is holy for בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: The פרה אדומה is not a מזבח offering. Its holiness is that of בדק הבית, which never makes a תמורה, so it gives no support.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is holy for בדק הבית, and things holy for בדק הבית do not make a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the פרה אדומה is not a true comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרה אדומה is not brought on the מזבח. Its holiness is the kind given to Temple upkeep, בדק הבית, and that kind of holiness cannot make a תמורה. So a female 'חטאת' of that type cannot give a female cow the status needed to make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Things made holy for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the מזבח
They do not make a תמורה

phrases.english: It is holy for Temple maintenance,
phrases.notes: "It" is the פרה אדומה, which is not offered on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: וְקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לָא עָבְדִי תְּמוּרָה.
phrases.english: and things holy for Temple maintenance do not make a תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the comparison does not fit, because the type of holiness is different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרה אדומה is a female חטאת, so a female set aside for any חטאת should make a תמורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרה אדומה has only בדק הבית holiness, which never makes a תמורה, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: The goats of an individual and of a נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a harder case: an individual's חטאת is a female goat and a נשיא's is a male goat, both real מזבח offerings. So swapping one for the other should make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An individual who set aside a male goat for his female goat: it should be holy, since there is the goat of the נשיא! Or, a נשיא who set aside a female goat for his male goat: it should be holy, since an individual sets aside a female goat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested reason again, this time with a case that the בדק הבית answer cannot solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both goats are real חטאת offerings on the מזבח: a regular person brings a female goat and a נשיא brings a male goat. By the suggested reason, a male set aside by an individual, or a female set aside by a נשיא, should carry חטאת status and make a תמורה. That does not seem to be רבי שמעון's view, so the reason is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: The female goat an ordinary person brings as a חטאת
The male goat a נשיא, a king or tribal leader, brings as a חטאת
Alternatively; or also

steps.whyThisMatters: Unlike the פרה אדומה, both goats are true מזבח offerings. So this challenge directly threatens the suggested reason for רבי שמעון's view.

phrases.english: An individual who set aside a male goat for his female goat —
let it be holy, since there is the male goat of the נשיא!

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, נָשִׂיא שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ שְׂעִירָה לִשְׂעִירוֹ —
phrases.english: Alternatively, a נשיא who set aside a female goat for his male goat —
let it be holy, since an individual sets aside a female goat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 answered the פרה אדומה challenge, this brings a new challenge to the step 7 reason, and the בדק הבית answer does not work here.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 7 reason: a female counts if any female version of the offering exists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The individual's goat and the נשיא's goat are both מזבח חטאת offerings of opposite sexes. So swapping one for the other should give חטאת status and make a תמורה.

steps.title: An individual and a נשיא are two different people
steps.stepSummary: The female goat of a יחיד and the male goat of a נשיא do not help each other, because they belong to two different kinds of people.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are two separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10. The female goat and the male goat belong to two different people, so one cannot give its status to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the פרה אדומה, the female was not a מזבח offering. Here both goats are real חטאות, so the גמרא needs a new reason. A female animal only counts as fit if the same person could bring a female, and a יחיד and a נשיא are different people with different obligations.

keyTerms.meaning: Two bodies, meaning two separate people or categories of people
An ordinary individual, whose חטאת is a female goat
The leader or king, whose חטאת is a male goat

phrases.english: These are two separate bodies.
phrases.notes: He means the יחיד and the נשיא from Step 10: two different people, so one's goat does not count for the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the goat challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the two offerings belong to different people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both goats are real מזבח חטאות, swapping a male for a female should count as a fit animal and make a תמורה
steps.terutzMaskana: A comparison only works within the same person; a יחיד's offering and a נשיא's offering belong to two different bodies

steps.title: What about someone who sinned before he became נשיא?
steps.stepSummary: A person sinned as a יחיד and later became נשיא. Now one body is involved, so a male goat set aside for his female-goat obligation should become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they sinned before they were appointed, then when he sets aside a male goat in place of his female goat, it should become holy, because if he sinned now he would be obligated to bring a male goat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'two bodies' answer with a case where it is the same person. He sinned while still a יחיד, became נשיא, and only then set aside a male goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two bodies' answer works when the people are different. Here it is one person, and today, as a נשיא, he is someone who brings a male goat. So the male goat should count as fit and become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: They were appointed, here as נשיא
Sets aside an animal for an offering
Now

phrases.english: If they sinned before they were appointed,
phrases.notes: He sinned while still a regular person, so he owes a female goat, and only later became נשיא.

phrases.english: when he sets aside a male goat in place of his female goat, it should become holy,
because if he sinned now,
he is someone who brings a male goat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'two bodies' answer of Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a יחיד and a נשיא are two separate bodies
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the same person was first a יחיד and is now a נשיא, there is only one body, and that person now brings male goats, so the male goat should count

steps.title: He never became obligated in a male goat
steps.stepSummary: His sin happened before he became נשיא, so his obligation was always a female goat, never a male one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did not sin now, so he was not obligated in a male goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that what matters is his status when he sinned. He sinned as a יחיד, so he was never obligated in a male goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a נשיא today does not matter for a sin committed earlier. His obligation was fixed when he sinned, and that obligation was a female goat. So the male goat is not a fit animal for his obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: He became obligated
But he did not sin, meaning not while he was a נשיא

phrases.english: But he did not sin now,
so he was not obligated in a male goat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא חָטָא לָא אִיחַיַּיב בְּשָׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the rule: what counts is the obligation the person actually has
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he is now a נשיא, a male goat is fit for him
steps.terutzMaskana: His obligation was set at the time of the sin, when he owed a female goat, so a male goat is not fit for him

steps.title: Then the bird עולה reason should not work either
steps.stepSummary: If what counts is the person's actual obligation, then a person who sets aside a female for an עולה is not bringing a bird עולה, so the bird עולה should not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, here too: he is not bringing a bird עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer against רבי שמעון's reason from Step 7. If we only look at the person's own obligation, this person is not bringing a bird עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said a female set aside for an עולה makes a תמורה because a bird עולה can be female. But Step 13 just taught that we only look at what this person is actually bringing. This person is not bringing a bird עולה, so that reason seems to fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Here too

phrases.english: If so, here too,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means רבי שמעון's case from Step 7: a female animal set aside for an עולה.

phrases.english: he is not bringing a bird burnt offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הָכָא נָמֵי, הָא לָאו עוֹלַת הָעוֹף קָמַיְיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 13 to challenge the reason given in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reason that a female for an עולה makes a תמורה because a bird עולה can be female
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the person's actual obligation counts, and this person is not obligated in a bird עולה, the bird עולה cannot make the female fit for him

steps.title: רבי שמעון holds that anyone may pledge a bird עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who says that anyone who pledges an עולה may bring a bird. So this person himself could bring a bird עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, as we learned in a משנה: one who says 'It is upon me to bring an עולה' must bring a lamb. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: or a turtledove or young pigeons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is a voluntary עולה. According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, anyone who pledges an עולה may bring a bird, so a bird עולה really is open to this person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that bird עולות are only for special obligations. But with a pledged עולה, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה lets anyone bring a turtledove or pigeons. So the same person could bring a bird עולה, which may be female, and the bird עולה reason stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is upon me to bring an עולה', a vow to bring a burnt offering
A lamb
A turtledove
Young pigeons

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, a female set aside for an עולה makes a תמורה because the owner himself could bring a female-type עולה: under רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, anyone who pledges an עולה may bring a bird.
steps.confusionAlert: The point is not that the female animal itself becomes a bird offering. The point is only that the same person could have brought an עולה that is female, a bird, so a female is a fit kind of עולה for him.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון holds it
like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה,
as we learned: 'It is upon me to bring a burnt offering' —
he must bring a lamb.
רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says:
or a turtledove or young pigeons.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14 and saves the reason of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking to another תנא's view: רבי שמעון follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only people with special obligations bring a bird עולה, so this person cannot bring one
steps.terutzMaskana: Anyone who pledges an עולה may bring a bird, so a bird עולה, which may be female, is open to this very person

steps.title: A משנה about dedicating all one's possessions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere about someone who dedicates all his possessions, and among them are male and female animals fit for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: someone dedicates all his possessions, and among them is an animal fit for the מזבח, males and females.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new source by quoting the case of a משנה from another place. The two opinions on this case come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man said only 'my possessions are holy.' He did not say for what purpose. His property includes animals that could be brought on the מזבח, both males and females, so we need to know what happens to them.

keyTerms.meaning: One who dedicates all his property to the בית המקדש
Fit to be brought as a קרבן on the מזבח
Male and female animals

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת שקלים (4:7).

phrases.english: One who dedicates his possessions,
and among them there was an animal
fit for the altar,
males and females.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new source, a משנה in שקלים, which the גמרא will use to keep discussing the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case: someone dedicates all his property without naming a purpose, and it includes male and female animals fit for the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: sell all the animals and give the money to בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the males are sold to people who need עולות, the females are sold to people who need שלמים, and all the money goes to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the males are sold for people who need עולות, and the females are sold for people who need שלמים. The money goes together with the rest of his property to the upkeep of the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first opinion on the case. רבי אליעזר treats the whole dedication as going to the upkeep fund, so the animals are sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the man did not say otherwise, רבי אליעזר holds that he meant everything for בדק הבית. The animals are still sold to people who will bring them as קרבנות: males for עולות and females for שלמים. Only the money goes to the upkeep fund.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offerings, which must be males and are completely burned on the מזבח
Peace offerings, which may be male or female
The fund for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
Their money value, the money received from selling them

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
the males should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings,
and the females should be sold for the needs of peace offerings,
and their money goes together with the rest of the possessions
to the upkeep of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first ruling on the case set up in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the animals are sold, males for עולות and females for שלמים, and the money goes to בדק הבית.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: males are brought as עולות, females are sold for שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the males themselves are brought as עולות. The females are sold for שלמים, and the money from them buys עולות. The rest of the property goes to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: the males themselves are brought as עולות. The females are sold for people who need שלמים, and with their money he brings עולות. The rest of the property goes to the upkeep of the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion. רבי יהושע assumes the man meant his animals as עולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע holds that the animals were meant for the מזבח as עולות. Males can be עולות, so they are brought as they are. Females cannot be עולות, so they are sold for שלמים, and their money is used to buy עולות. Only the property that is not fit for the מזבח goes to בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: Themselves, meaning the actual animals and not their money
They are brought as קרבנות on the מזבח
The rest of the property, the things that are not fit for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע treats the man's animals as meant for עולות. The females can't be עולות, so they are sold for שלמים and the money buys עולות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
the males themselves are brought as burnt offerings,
and the females are sold for the needs of peace offerings,
and with their money he brings burnt offerings,
and the rest of the possessions go to the upkeep of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing ruling to רבי אליעזר's view in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The males are brought as עולות, the females are sold for שלמים and their money buys עולות, and the remaining property goes to בדק הבית.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא asks how the females can become שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא asks רבי יוחנן: according to רבי יהושע, the females were dedicated as עולות, which they can never be. So their holiness was pushed aside. How can they then be brought as שלמים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to רבי יוחנן: according to רבי יהושע, who says the males themselves are brought as עולות, how can the females be brought as שלמים? They come from a holiness that was pushed aside!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא challenges רבי יהושע's ruling about the females.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע says the owner meant his animals as עולות. A female dedicated as an עולה can never be brought, so her holiness is 'pushed aside' (דחויה). Normally an animal like that is not brought on the מזבח at all, so it is hard to see how the buyer can bring her as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness that was pushed aside, a dedication that could not be carried out
By the power of, coming from
How?
They come (from)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that females can't be שלמים, because they can. The problem is that these particular females were first dedicated as עולות, which they could never be.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge raises whether an animal whose first dedication failed can still be used for a different קרבן. That question ties into the larger discussion here about animals set aside for one purpose being used for another.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Yochanan:
According to Rabbi Yehoshua, who said
the males themselves are brought as burnt offerings,
how can the females be brought as peace offerings?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Either way, he's asking how they can be שלמים.

phrases.english: They come from a holiness that was pushed aside!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי (מקרבן) [קָרְבָן] שְׁלָמִים? הָא מִכֹּחַ קְדוּשָּׁה דְּחוּיָּיה קָאָתְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the part of רבי יהושע's ruling in step 18 about the females.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling that the females are sold to be brought as שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the owner meant the animals as עולות, the females' holiness as עולות was pushed aside, since they can never be עולות. An animal with pushed-aside holiness should not be brought on the מזבח, even as a שלמים.

steps.title: Another version: if the males are holy in body, why are the females sold right away?
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the question, רבי חייא בר אבא reasons that רבי יהושע must hold the animals got קדושת הגוף. If so, the females should need to graze until blemished, not be sold right away for שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: רבי חייא בר אבא said to רבי יוחנן: Since רבי יהושע said the males themselves are brought as עולות, does that mean the animals were made holy with holiness of the body itself? If so, why are the females sold for שלמים? They should need to graze until they get a blemish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא retells רבי חייא בר אבא's question in a different form. Now the question starts from the males and asks why the females are not treated the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing the males straight onto the מזבח shows the owner's dedication gave them קדושת הגוף. If the females got that same kind of holiness, they could not be sold while unblemished. They would have to graze until they get a מום. So selling them right away for שלמים seems inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same discussion
Holiness of the animal's body itself, not just of its money value
Is that to say? (introduces a conclusion drawn from a statement)
Grazing: leaving a holy animal to graze until it gets a blemish

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the same question as Step 19, told another way. In Step 19 the difficulty was that the females' holiness was 'pushed aside'. Here the difficulty is that the females should need to graze.

phrases.english: Another version:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Yochanan:
From the fact that Rabbi Yehoshua said
the males themselves are brought as burnt offerings,
is that to say he made them holy with holiness of the body?
If so, why are the females
sold for the needs of peace offerings?
It needs grazing!
phrases.notes: It should be left to graze until it gets a blemish, and only then be sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחְרִינָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second version of the challenge in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling that the females are sold for שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Males brought as עולות means the dedication gave them קדושת הגוף. Then the females would have it too, and they would need to graze until blemished instead of being sold.

steps.title: רבי יהושע follows רבי שמעון: unfit animals get no body-holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that רבי יהושע agrees with רבי שמעון. An animal that is not fit to be brought itself does not get קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יהושע holds like רבי שמעון, who said: anything that is not fit to be brought itself does not get holiness of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. The females were never fit to be עולות, so they never got body-holiness, and they can be sold right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The males are fit for עולות, so the dedication made their bodies holy. The females cannot be עולות, so only their value became holy. Because there is no קדושת הגוף, they do not need to graze until blemished.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (agrees with the opinion of)
Fit for itself, meaning the animal itself can be brought as that offering
Descends, takes hold (said of holiness)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key rule: body-holiness only takes hold when the animal is fit for the use it was dedicated to.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Yehoshua
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is the one answering here.

phrases.english: holds like Rabbi Shimon,
who said: anything
that is not fit in itself,
holiness of the body does not take hold of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the ruling to a known opinion (רבי שמעון) with a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The females, like the males, got קדושת הגוף and need to graze until blemished
steps.terutzMaskana: The females were never fit for an עולה, so they got only money-holiness and can be sold right away

steps.title: Proof from רבי שמעון's ruling on a female set aside for an אשם
steps.stepSummary: The source is a משנה where רבי שמעון rules that a female set aside for an אשם may be sold without a blemish. The reason is that a female is not fit for an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי שמעון says it may be sold without a blemish. And we said that רבי שמעון's reason is that since a female is not fit for an אשם, body-holiness does not take hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings the source for רבי שמעון's rule. It is a case of a female animal set aside for an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם must be a male. So when someone sets aside a female for one, רבי שמעון lets it be sold even while unblemished. This shows that an unfit animal only gets holiness of its value, which matches the females in our case.

keyTerms.meaning: It may be sold without a blemish
The reason

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Shimon says:
it may be sold without a blemish,
phrases.notes: This is about a female animal someone set aside for an אשם.

phrases.english: and we said that Rabbi Shimon's reason is
since a female is not fit for a guilt offering,
holiness of the body does not take hold of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule given in Step 21
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's rule that an unfit animal gets no קדושת הגוף
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבי שמעון rules that a female set aside for an אשם is sold without a blemish

steps.title: Pushback: maybe רבי שמעון only said this about a female for an אשם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to question the proof. Perhaps רבי שמעון's rule applies only to a female set aside for an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that רבי שמעון said this about a female for an אשם,
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's comparison to רבי שמעון. This line sets up a contrast, and the rest of it continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection suggests that the אשם case may be special. Maybe it cannot be stretched to our case of someone who dedicates all his possessions. The full reason for the difference comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, grant that (introduces a limit: 'fine, he said it there, but...')
Regarding, in the case of

phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Shimon said this
regarding a female for a guilt offering,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן גַּבֵּי נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to reject the proof brought in Step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a female set aside for an אשם and the females in our case of someone who dedicates all his possessions
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי שמעון's rule may be limited to a female set aside for an אשם (the full distinction comes next)
